derivation: from a compound of G2342 (θηρίον) and G3164 (μάχομαι);
def: to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men)

occurrences.text: If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
